newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MAN WHO HELPED CHANGE FACE OF BRITISH SOCCER DIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MAN WHO HELPED CHANGE FACE OF BRITISH SOCCER DIES.

text.p: Former Lord Chief Justice Lord Taylor, who headed the inquiry into the Hillsborough football stadium disaster, has died of cancer. He was 66. Lord Taylor retired early from his post in March last year after his illness was diagnosed. He underwent radiotherapy but doctors could not save him.
Prime Minister John Major paid tribute to Lord Taylor on Tuesday saying: "This is very sad news. He was a very fine man."

Lord Taylor's inquiry, which followed the 1989 Hillsborough disaster in which 96 Liverpool fans were crushed to death in an over-crowded, fenced-in, standing section of the ground, helped to change the face of British soccer.
In many stadiums 80-year-old terraced areas were replaced by new modern seating areas, while in some cases the old stadiums were knocked down completely and replaced by new all-seater grounds.
